critic_notes.target_name: External Funding Load on Fixed Investment
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially a mechanical product of two well-documented anomalies (asset/PP&E growth and net external financing, Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan), and scaling financing by capex rather than assets introduces a near-zero, sign-unstable denominator for asset-light firms that winsorization only partly tames, so the incremental content over the known composite is thin.

The multiplicative cash-decline INDICATOR zeroes out roughly half the cross-section, so the "short" leg is a genuine high-growth/high-issuance group while the "long" leg is an undifferentiated mass of ties at zero, making the portfolio spread an artifact of the dummy rather than a test of the stated warehoused-proceeds mechanism.

Because non-issuers are collapsed to zero below all issuers, the signal's cross-sectional variation is dominated by the net-share-issuance dummy (a known anomaly) rather than by capex acceleration, so the interaction as coded cannot isolate the hypothesized timing channel.

Economically coherent leveraged-empire-building interaction with a correctly signed monotone construction and no degenerate indicator, though aqc and Δgdwl are largely redundant and the mass of zero-acquisition firms will concentrate ties in the low leg.

Combining real operating-capacity expansion (inventory plus headcount) with short-maturity financing is a substantively different rollover-risk/fragility mechanism rather than a repackaging of asset growth, and the expression's direction matches the stated negative sign.

The signed funding-source contrast scaled by capex intensity is internally consistent with the positive expected sign, but Δcash and external issuance are mechanically positively correlated so the two legs largely duplicate one another, leaving the signal close to a capex-weighted restatement of the external financing anomaly and vulnerable to cash burn being read as "deployment."

This is essentially the archive's "Continuous Warehoused-Proceeds Deployment" with asset growth swapped for capex and the cash-deployment leg folded into the same rank — a cosmetic recombination of already-tested lagged-financing/cash-drawdown components rather than a new mechanism.

A 3-year smoothed conjunction of capex/assets and net external financing is little more than the published net-external-financing and investment anomalies averaged together, and it adds no economic content beyond the already-tested investment×financing bottleneck signals.

The intangible-expansion leg is a genuinely new component in this pair's archive and the equity-timing conjunction is economically coherent, though `intan` sparsity and its acquisition-driven overlap with goodwill growth warrant a coverage check.

Gross-PPE expansion conditioned on a short-versus-long debt maturity tilt introduces a financing-fragility dimension absent from prior proposals, and the expression's natural direction matches the stated negative sign, though the sign could plausibly reverse if maturity mismatch proxies for compensated risk.

The inventory-minus-PPE difference is not identifying what the hypothesis claims — firms with flat inventory but contracting PP&E score high on that leg — so the signal's long leg will mix genuine inventory gluts with capital-shrinking issuers, muddying interpretation of any result.

Re-expressing the archive's strongest components as within-firm time-series extremes is a substantive, diagnostically motivated change rather than a cosmetic variant, but the 5-period TS_RANK window is coarse and may induce heavy ties and unstable portfolio composition.

This is essentially a re-normalization of the archived "Firm-Specific Funding and Investment Peaks" (deviation-from-own-3yr-MA in place of TS_RANK over the same investment and external-financing constructs), i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

It is the archived "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck" with the cash-retention leg — the component that plausibly drove that signal's strength — removed and total external financing merely split into its equity and debt halves, so it is a weaker rediscovery of an already-evaluated construct (and of the well-known composite external-financing anomaly).

Internally consistent and a genuine funding-channel switch relative to the archived debt-funded hiring signal, though the equity-issuance level gate and the equity-minus-debt tilt are largely redundant with each other and the components (employee growth, net share issuance) are individually well-documented anomalies.

Introduces a genuinely new conditioning dimension (pre-existing balance-sheet capacity, correctly lagged to avoid mechanical contamination) rather than recombining the same investment-financing pair, and the expected negative sign is coherent with both the leverage puzzle and investment-overextension logic.

The simultaneous-issuance-and-distribution conjunction is a legitimately novel angle, but the payout leg is a well-established *positive* return predictor pulling against the stated negative sign, so the composite's expected direction is theoretically ambiguous and the gross-flow terms will tilt toward large mature firms.

"Stock-financed acquirers underperform" is a textbook published anomaly (Loughran-Vijh, Rau-Vermaelen) built from two individually known effects (goodwill/acquisition intensity and net share issuance), and it closely echoes the archived Debt-Funded Acquisition Footprint with the financing leg simply swapped.

This is essentially the archived "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck" with the (Δppent+Δinvt) sum decomposed into two separate MIN legs — a cosmetic reparameterization that will mainly shrink the intersection tail and coverage rather than test a new mechanism.

Adding a current-capex leg to the archived "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" is an incremental fourth AND-condition on an already narrow ~9% coverage intersection, so it is a variant rather than a substantively different hypothesis and risks unstable portfolio composition.

The switch to balance-sheet liability and equity changes is a genuinely different, higher-coverage financing channel than the archive's cash-flow issuance fields, though it is partly mechanical (Δat ≈ Δlt + Δceq) and the Δceq leg conflates value-destroying losses with return-enhancing repurchases, muddying the expected sign.

This is the archived "Low-Liquidity Debt-Funded Inventory Build" with the inventory leg swapped for the intangible leg from "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" — a one-field substitution mash-up of two already-evaluated signals rather than a new interaction.

The employment leg already delivered a wrong-signed FF5 alpha (+1.5%) in "Debt-Funded Organizational Expansion," and stacking sparsely reported emp growth with inventory and liability growth in a triple MIN mainly compounds coverage and composition instability without a new economic mechanism.

Replacing the archived payout *level* leg with a payout *contraction* leg is a real change of mechanism (funding stress rather than capital recycling) and the gross-issuance choice is a thoughtful guard against mechanical overlap, though the Δ(prstkc+dvc) term is extremely lumpy and partially overlaps the known payout/repurchase-cut literature.

This is a cosmetic one-leg swap of the archived "Rollover-Funded Capital Spending" (capx replaced by the PP&E+inventory deployment term already used in "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck"), recombining two existing components without a new mechanism, and the gross issuance/retirement double-gate mostly proxies for size/debt-intensity rather than genuine rollover stress.

Identical three-way structure to the archived "Overlevered Debt-Funded Capex Ramp" with only the investment leg swapped to the same PP&E+inventory measure used elsewhere in the archive, so it is a variant rather than a diagnosis-driven redesign of why that signal's FMB slope had the wrong sign.

The conditioning on *prior* net PP&E contraction reverses (rather than repeats) the archived "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" sequencing and is internally consistent, though the sign is economically ambiguous since post-contraction rebuilds could equally reflect cheap, recovering assets, and the core ingredients remain the well-known investment and net-external-financing anomalies.

The residual (asset growth minus tangible deployment) decomposition with a total-growth gate is a legitimately new construction that guards against the contraction artifact, but it is close to a refinement of the published asset-growth anomaly and its residual leg is contaminated by cash accumulation, which works against the stated "opaque deployment" mechanism.

The debt-versus-equity funding flip relative to the archived "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" is a substantive rather than cosmetic change, the level gate correctly prevents buyback-driven false positives, and the collateralizability mismatch story is coherent—though intan-based coverage and the archived signal's near-zero alpha temper expectations.

Requiring equity issuance *and* net debt retirement alongside expansion is a genuinely different financing-composition test (net external financing is roughly neutral, so it is not a rediscovery of the composite-issuance anomaly), but it is structurally close to "Equity-Heavy Workforce Scaling," which was weak, and the triple hard gate risks a thin, unstable long leg.

This is a one-leg swap on the archived "Maturity-Wall Investment Commitment" that merely bolts on the DELTA(che) cash-depletion term already recycled through four archived signals, so it is an incremental respecification rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing the financing level with its first difference is a genuine economic change (unexpected funding need vs. habitual issuer) rather than a cosmetic tweak, and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it remains a close descendant of "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" and inherits its lagged-investment/cash-drain scaffolding wholesale.

Subtracting cash growth from an already-computed residual is a marginal redefinition of the archived "Liability-Funded Opaque Asset Expansion," whose portfolio alpha was significantly *opposite* in sign (+2.6 t-stat) — a tweak of this size is very unlikely to flip that, and the construct is in any case dominated by the published asset-growth/NOA anomalies.

Swapping the lagged cash *level* for the contemporaneous cash *change* leaves the archived "Low-Liquidity Debt-Funded Inventory Build" otherwise intact, and the resulting triple (inventory up, debt issued, cash down) is close to a sources-and-uses accounting tautology rather than an independent conditioning insight.

A three-year TREND substituted for a one-year DELTA is precisely the kind of cosmetic smoothing variant that should not be re-tested on a parent signal whose long-short alpha was economically negligible (0.004) with a t-stat of 0.44.

The wedge between share-count growth and cash raised from stock sales is a genuinely new construct in this archive with coherent sign logic, but it overlaps materially with the published composite-share-issuance anomaly and GROWTH(csho) is contaminated by splits and stock dividends that 1% winsorization will not remove, so measurement hygiene must be checked before crediting any result.

This is a MIN→MUL reparameterization of the archive's "Termed-Out Investment Financing" using the identical three inputs and mechanism, and the multiplicative form additionally collapses all low-capex firms toward zero so the maturity contrast is only informative in the high-capex tail — a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

The maturity-matching interaction (Myers-style duration alignment) is a genuinely novel, well-motivated test rather than a known anomaly, though the symmetric product means the high-signal leg also contains inventory-building/short-debt firms whose level effects historically predict *low* returns, so an unconditional level confound may blunt or invert the expected positive sign.

The "aligned" high end explicitly contains intangible-expansion-plus-net-equity-issuance firms, which the archive's "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" already found to predict *lower* returns (fmb −4.37), so the expression's natural direction contradicts the stated positive expected sign.

Same three inputs and mechanism as the archive's "Externally Funded Inventory-Workforce Divergence," rewritten from a MIN intersection to a rank contrast weighted by financing intensity; the stated diagnosis (sparse intersection) is reasonable but the result is a reparameterization with little new economic content, and the nonnegative financing weight leaves low-financing firms undifferentiated in the middle.

Nearly identical to the archive's "Equity-Proceeds Book-Capital Leakage" (capex × net equity issuance × failure of equity to build book capital), with the third leg swapped for a change in ceq/at that is largely mechanically implied by the leverage/asset growth already embedded in the first two legs.

This is the exact mirror of the archive's "Debt-Then-Equity Funding Escalation" (same three legs with the debt/equity lags swapped), the ordering rationale is asserted rather than derived and is not actually encoded beyond a one-period lag, and the signal remains a low-coverage triple intersection of three already-known issuance/investment anomalies.

This is essentially the archived "Maturity-Wall Investment Commitment" with the third leg swapped from debt-stock growth to net equity issuance — a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested legs (capx×equity issuance appears in at least four archived variants with near-zero alpha), and the stated "forced dilution" mechanism is not separately identified by an unconditional MIN of ranks.

The expression is internally consistent and the low-prior-leverage conditioning is a substantive sign-flip of the archived "Overlevered Debt-Funded Capex Ramp" rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the positive expected sign fights the well-documented negative base effects of both investment and debt issuance, so the burden of proof is high.

Requiring low net debt issuance plus net repurchases is largely a rediscovery of the net-share-issuance/payout anomaly, and the construction is a close cousin of the archived "Deleveraging Productive Expansion" and "Equity-Funded Deleveraging Expansion" with the financing legs simply re-signed.

The maturity-shortening-during-a-maturity-event mechanism is coherent, sign-consistent with the expression, and distinguishable from the weak archived "Short-Maturity Fixed-Investment Mismatch", but it is close to the mirror image of the already-tested "Termed-Out Investment Financing", so the informational gain is incremental.

This is the sign-flipped mirror of the archived "External Funding Excess Over Capex" (investment-minus-financing gap with an investment floor), and because the second leg is itself monotonically increasing in investment the composite is largely a repackaged investment/asset-growth measure whose natural direction opposes the stated positive expected sign.

Adding a tangibility (debt-capacity) condition to the archived "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" is an economically motivated refinement that sharpens the market-timing interpretation rather than a mechanical third leg, though the near-orthogonality of high PP&E intensity and rapid intangible growth risks a thin, unstable long leg.

This is a one-leg cosmetic substitution (capx → ΔPPEGT) on the already-tested "Termed-Out Investment Financing," keeping the same net-LT-issuance and falling-short-debt legs and the same mechanism, so it is a near-rediscovery rather than a substantive refinement.

Identical in structure and mechanism to the archived "Deleveraging Productive Expansion" with only the investment proxy swapped from ΔPPENT+ΔINVT to ΔPPEGT, and the parent already showed economically negligible alpha (0.004, t=0.47), so the variant is both derivative and unpromising.

The economics (unused secured debt capacity) are coherent, but the construction merely stacks the legs of two already-tested signals into a four-way MIN of ranks, which mechanically collapses to the weakest leg, concentrates the long portfolio in a thin, tangible-heavy/low-leverage subset, and risks apparent gains from unstable composition rather than a new mechanism.

Direct re-proposal of the archived "Maturity-Downgrade Investment" with capx replaced by ΔPPEGT while the two financing legs are unchanged, so it adds no new economic content beyond a proxy substitution.

Beyond being a bolt-together of two archive signals, the third leg is mechanically collinear with the second (same numerator) and its high values mostly identify firms with negative retained earnings, so the signal largely re-expresses the known loss-firm/low-profitability anomaly rather than a novel financing-investment interaction.

Substituting the within-firm inventory level state for the inventory flow in the archived "Externally Funded Inventory-Workforce Divergence" is economically defensible (unsold stock during retrenchment vs. growth investment), but it remains a single-leg variant of an already-evaluated signal and inherits its weak cross-sectional evidence (fmb t = 0.51), so it does not constitute a substantively different improvement.

This is a mechanical union of two archived signals — the gen-8 "Broad-Scope Externally Funded Expansion" (legs 1–2 verbatim) plus the gen-0 "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck" cash-deployment leg (leg 3 verbatim) — so it is a recombination rather than a new mechanism, and both parents already sit squarely on the known asset-growth / net-external-financing anomaly.

The first two legs replicate the archive's strongest signal, but substituting the debt-retirement burden for the cash-deployment leg is a genuinely different economic condition (refinancing pressure rather than capital deployment), the sign is internally consistent, and it is testable — though the risk is that a weakly informative maturity leg simply dilutes an already-strong parent.

This is essentially "Simultaneous Capex-Leverage Peaks" (gen 8) stapled to the financing legs of "Maturity-Downgrade Investment" (gen 7) with a SUMRANK softening, which the reasoning itself concedes, making it a cosmetic recombination whose parents each delivered only marginal alpha.

It merges two archived positive-sign signals ("Balance-Sheet-Slack Debt Investment" and "Termed-Out Investment Financing"), but the soft SUMRANK of unused debt capacity and maturity improvement is a coherent joint "financing quality" construct with a consistent expected sign and two independently supportive parents, so it is worth one test even though it is close to a merge.

This is the gen-2 "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" with the hard cash-depletion leg softened by averaging in a leverage TS_RANK — a cosmetic variant that is unlikely to repair the parent's weak Fama-MacBeth slope, since softening a leg typically blurs rather than sharpens cross-sectional identification.

It fuses two archived signals whose FMB slopes and FF5 alphas already pointed in opposite directions (gen-7 and gen-8 both had positive t-stats with negative alphas), and the third leg subtracts a share-count growth rate from a change in an equity ratio — badly mismatched scales, so the rank is effectively driven by dilution alone rather than the stated joint condition.
